Logistics Systems with Strictly Uniform Rational Output ​

Source page ID: 0WLX026mkdC5fBsqYZDI00 | Open in Tencent Docs

This subdocument was completed by @桜夜天華.

Events ​

A single passage of an item through a port is called an event. Passage through an input port is an input event; passage through an output port is an output event.

Game ticks (tick) ​

The Talos-II logistics system uses ticks as its discrete time unit. This article treats one tick as the basic time step for updating logistics-system states and determining events. In actual operation, 1tick≈2s, but server latency and other factors may introduce a deviation of about 1s in real time.

Event sequences ​

Because time is discrete in ticks, a binary sequence can record whether an event occurs at a given port in each tick. This is called an event sequence, denoted by

X=X1X2X3…,Xt∈{0,1}.

Here, Xt=1 means an event occurs at that port in tick t; Xt=0 means no event occurs there in tick t.

For an input port, this is called the input sequence, denoted by

I=I1I2I3…,It∈{0,1}.

Here, It=1 means an item enters in tick t; It=0 means no item enters in tick t.

For an output port, this is called the output sequence, denoted by

O=O1O2O3…,Ot∈{0,1}.

Here, Ot=1 means an item exits in tick t; Ot=0 means no item exits in tick t.

Range of event intervals ​

For any event sequence, the ticks satisfying Xt=1 are its event times. Arrange them in increasing order as

τ1<τ2<τ3<⋯.

Here, τk​ is the tick of the kth event, satisfying Xτk=1.

The difference between consecutive event times is called the event interval, defined by

Δk=τk+1−τk.

When X is an input sequence, τk is an input time and Δk is an input interval. The corresponding terminology applies to output.

Consider the set of all event intervals,

D={Δk}.

The range of this event sequence is defined by

R=supkΔk−infkΔk.

Within a finite observation window, it can also be written as

R=maxkΔk−minkΔk.

Range of cumulative counts ​

Let the event sequence be

X=X1X2X3…,Xt∈{0,1}.

For any positive integer L, define the cumulative event count in a window of length L starting at tick i as

CL(i)=∑t=ii+L−1Xt.

Here, CL(i) is the total number of events in this window of length L.

For fixed window length L, define the range of length-L cumulative counts of the event sequence as

QL=maxiCL(i)−miniCL(i).

Uniformity ​

If the interval range of an event sequence satisfies

R≤1,

then the event sequence is called uniform. In other words, the intervals between consecutive events differ by at most one tick.

Strict uniformity (Beatty-1 uniformity) ​

For every window length

L∈Z>0

if an event sequence satisfies

QL≤1,

then the event sequence is called strictly uniform.

Duty cycle ​

The duty cycle describes the mean event frequency within a time window. For a contiguous window of length L starting at tick i, it is defined by

dL(i)=1L∑t=ii+L−1Xt.

The duty cycle can also be understood as the average number of input or output items per tick over a period. When X=I, dL(i) is the input duty cycle; when X=O, dL(i) is the output duty cycle.

Full belts ​

If an event sequence has an event in every tick, that is,

Xt=1,∀t∈Z>0,

then it is called a full belt. A full belt means items continuously pass through the corresponding port, with duty cycle d=1.

n-thinned sequences ​

Let the event sequence be

X=(Xt)t≥1,Xt∈{0,1}.

Denote its event times by

τ1<τ2<τ3<⋯,Xτk=1.

For any positive integer n, define the sequence

Y(n)=(Yt(n))t≥1

by

Yt(n)={1,t=τ1+qn,q=0,1,2,…,0,otherwise.

In other words, starting with the first event, retain one event out of every n events and set the remaining events to 0.

We call Y(n) the n-thinned sequence of X.

Logistics components ​

Any machine with input ports, output ports and storage capacity can be called a logistics component. A component with m input ports and n output ports is called an m-input, n-output component.

Blocking (?) ​

Consider a logistics component whose storage has reached capacity. Let its input duty cycles be

di.

If

∑di≥1,

then the logistics component is said to be blocked. Its output duty cycle is then

dout=1.

Round-robin servicing (?) ​

Suppose a logistics component has n equivalent ports. If, for any K consecutive pending events in the event sequence,

the event count at each port belongs to

{⌊Kn⌋,⌈Kn⌉},

then the component is called round-robin.

Logistics systems ​

Equilibrium ​

If a logistics system satisfies the following conditions:

(1) No items are created or destroyed inside the system;(2) Internal stored quantity Bt neither accumulates nor runs a deficit over the long term;

that is, constants Bmin and Bmax exist such that for any t,

Bmin≤Bt≤Bmax,

then the logistics system is said to be in equilibrium.

Conservation of duty cycle ​

The input duty cycle of a logistics system in equilibrium must equal its output duty cycle.

Splitters (in the broad sense) ​

A splitter is a logistics structure that lowers the effective output duty cycle of an individual branch through round-robin distribution.

The basic idea is to feed an incoming item stream into a logistics component with multiple equivalent output ports, distributing input events among the outputs according to the round-robin rule. Since each output receives only a fraction of the total incoming stream, each output port has a lower effective output duty cycle than the total input duty cycle.

When a splitter is in equilibrium, the quantity stored inside the system is 0.

Flow limiters ​

A flow limiter is a logistics structure that lowers the effective input duty cycle through blocking feedback.

The basic idea is to return feedback output from the downstream system to the limiting structure. Feedback items compete with upstream input items for limited transmission capacity, periodically blocking some upstream input events and ultimately reducing the effective input duty cycle entering the downstream system.

When a flow limiter is in equilibrium, its internal storage is at capacity.

Strictly uniform output structures ​

n-thinning (xn,x∈[0,1],n∈Z>0) ​

Suppose the event sequence

X=(Xt)t≥1,Xt∈{0,1},

is strictly uniform. Then its n-thinned sequence Y(n) is also strictly uniform.

Proof ​

For any window length L, denote the cumulative event count of X in the window starting at tick i,

of length L, by

CLX(i)=∑t=ii+L−1Xt.

Since X is strictly uniform, for any L,

maxiCLX(i)−miniCLX(i)≤1.

Therefore, an integer aL exists such that for any i,

CLX(i)∈{aL,aL+1}.

Now consider that same window of length L. Suppose it contains m

events of X, that is,

m=CLX(i).

Their indices in the original event sequence must be consecutive. Denote those indices by

p+1,p+2,…,p+m.

By the definition of an n-thinned sequence, Y(n) retains events whose indices satisfy

k≡r(modn)

Thus, the cumulative event count of Y(n) in this window is the number of integers in the consecutive interval

{p+1,p+2,…,p+m}

belonging to the congruence class r(modn).

Among any m consecutive integers, the number belonging to a fixed congruence class modulo n can only be

⌊mn⌋or⌈mn⌉.

Hence

CLY(i)=∑t=ii+L−1Yt(n)∈{⌊mn⌋,⌈mn⌉}.

Also, since

m∈{aL,aL+1},

all possible values of CLY(i) belong to

{⌊aLn⌋,⌈aLn⌉,⌊aL+1n⌋,⌈aL+1n⌉}.

Therefore, for any window length L,

maxiCLY(i)−miniCLY(i)≤⌈aL+1n⌉−⌊aLn⌋≤1.

That is,

QL(Y(n))≤1,∀L∈Z>0.

Thus, Y(n) is strictly uniform.

Merging full belts followed by n-thinning (r+xn,x∈[0,1],n,r∈Z>0,n>r) ​

Strict uniformity is preserved under the logistics operation of merging full belts and outputting in round-robin order. When multiple such components are cascaded, strict uniformity can propagate stage by stage to subsequent outputs, provided every stage obeys the round-robin rule.

Suppose the input sequence

X=X1X2X3…,Xt∈{0,1},

is strictly uniform. Feed X together with r full belts into a round-robin logistics component with n equivalent output ports, where 0≤r≤n−1.

Then all n output sequences of this component,

Y(1),Y(2),…,Y(n)

are strictly uniform.

Proof ​

For input sequence X, define the cumulative event count in a window of length L by

CL(i)=∑t=ii+L−1Xt.

Since X is strictly uniform, for any positive integer L,

maxiCL(i)−miniCL(i)≤1.

Therefore, an integer aL exists such that for any starting time i,

CL(i)∈{aL,aL+1}.

Now consider that same time window of length L. Besides X, the system receives

r full belts. Each full belt inputs L items within a window of length L,

so the total input event count in this window is

AL(i)=rL+CL(i).

From CL(i)∈{aL,aL+1}, we obtain

AL(i)∈{rL+aL, rL+aL+1}.

Write

KL=rL+aL,

Then

AL(i)∈{KL,KL+1}.

Let the cumulative output count at output port j within the window of length L starting at tick i be

BL(j)(i)=∑t=ii+L−1Yt(j).

Since the component is round-robin, for any output port j,

BL(j)(i)∈{⌊AL(i)n⌋,⌈AL(i)n⌉}.

Together with

AL(i)∈{KL,KL+1},

this shows that all possible values of BL(j)(i) belong to

{⌊KLn⌋,⌈KLn⌉,⌊KL+1n⌋,⌈KL+1n⌉}.

Therefore, for any output port j and any window length L,

maxiBL(j)(i)−miniBL(j)(i)≤⌈KL+1n⌉−⌊KLn⌋≤1.

That is,

QL(Y(j))≤1,∀L∈Z>0.

By the definition of strict uniformity, Y(j) is strictly uniform.

Logistics systems with strictly uniform rational output ​

Recursive splitting of the r+xn type ​

An m-input, n-output logistics component can transform the duty cycle according to

di=r+di−1n,di∈[0,1],m,n∈Z+,r∈N,n>m>r.

Here, r means merging r full belts, and di−1 is the input stream from the preceding stage.

Each transformation is called one splitting stage.

Consider a closed-loop feedback stream x, and set d0=x. If we consider only Protocol Stashes, then m,n≤3.

We need a decomposition (ri,ni) of the target duty cycle such that

x=A+xB,

while satisfying

B=∏ini,A=∑iri∏j<inj

The Python code follows (generated by ChatGPT 5.5 Thinking):

plaintext
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

"""
duty_synth.py

Given a target duty ratio x = p/q, synthesize a feedback construction

    u_i = (r_i + u_{i-1}) / n_i,
    u_k = u_0 = x,

where each pair (r_i, n_i) means:
    - merge r_i full belts and the current stream u_{i-1};
    - feed them into an n_i-output round-robin element;
    - take one output as u_i.

The construction uses only elements with:
    r_i + 1 <= max_inputs,
    n_i <= max_outputs.

Default: max_inputs = max_outputs = 3.

The closed-loop value is

    x = A / (B - 1),

where

    B = product_i n_i,
    A = r_1 + r_2 n_1 + r_3 n_1 n_2 + ... .

Therefore, to realize p/q, we search for B such that

    B == 1 mod q,

then set

    A = p (B - 1) / q,

and expand A in the mixed radix bases n_1, ..., n_k.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
from collections import deque
from fractions import Fraction
from functools import reduce
from operator import mul
from typing import List, Tuple, Optional


Pair = Tuple[int, int]  # (r_i, n_i)


def product(xs: List[int]) -> int:
    return reduce(mul, xs, 1)


def parse_fraction(s: str) -> Fraction:
    """
    Parse strings such as:
        325/799
        0.5
        1
    """
    try:
        x = Fraction(s)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"Cannot parse duty cycle: {s}") from exc

    if x < 0 or x > 1:
        raise ValueError("The target duty cycle must satisfy 0 <= x <= 1.")

    return x


def reconstruct_sequence(
    parent: dict[int, Optional[int]],
    action: dict[int, int],
    last_residue: int,
    last_base: int,
    start: int,
) -> List[int]:
    """
    Reconstruct a base sequence after finding:
        last_residue * last_base == start mod q.
    """
    seq = [last_base]
    cur = last_residue

    while cur != start:
        seq.append(action[cur])
        cur = parent[cur]

    seq.reverse()
    return seq


def find_shortest_base_cycle(q: int, allowed_bases: List[int]) -> Optional[List[int]]:
    """
    Find the shortest non-empty sequence n_1, ..., n_k such that

        product_i n_i == 1 mod q.

    This is a BFS over residues modulo q.
    """
    if q <= 0:
        raise ValueError("q must be positive.")

    start = 1 % q

    bases = [n for n in allowed_bases if math.gcd(n, q) == 1]

    if not bases:
        return None

    parent: dict[int, Optional[int]] = {start: None}
    action: dict[int, int] = {}
    depth: dict[int, int] = {start: 0}

    queue: deque[int] = deque([start])

    while queue:
        cur = queue.popleft()

        for n in bases:
            nxt = (cur * n) % q

            # Found a non-empty cycle back to 1 mod q.
            if nxt == start:
                return reconstruct_sequence(
                    parent=parent,
                    action=action,
                    last_residue=cur,
                    last_base=n,
                    start=start,
                )

            if nxt not in parent:
                parent[nxt] = cur
                action[nxt] = n
                depth[nxt] = depth[cur] + 1
                queue.append(nxt)

    return None


def mixed_radix_digits_low_to_high(A: int, bases: List[int]) -> List[int]:
    """
    For recurrence

        u_i = (r_i + u_{i-1}) / n_i,

    the constant term is

        A = r_1 + r_2 n_1 + r_3 n_1 n_2 + ...

    So digits must be extracted from low to high:
        r_1 = A mod n_1,
        r_2 = floor(A / n_1) mod n_2,
        ...
    """
    digits: List[int] = []
    x = A

    for n in bases:
        digits.append(x % n)
        x //= n

    if x != 0:
        raise RuntimeError("Mixed-radix expansion failed: A is outside the range of the product of the specified bases.")

    return digits


def synthesize_feedback(
    target: Fraction,
    max_inputs: int = 3,
    max_outputs: int = 3,
) -> List[Pair]:
    """
    Synthesize pairs (r_i, n_i).

    To guarantee r_i + 1 <= max_inputs for all possible digits,
    we conservatively use bases

        n_i <= min(max_inputs, max_outputs).

    This is sufficient for the m,n <= 3 case.
    """
    if max_inputs < 2 or max_outputs < 2:
        raise ValueError("max_inputs and max_outputs must both be at least 2.")

    if target == 0:
        # x = x / 2 has fixed point x = 0.
        return [(0, 2)]

    if target == 1:
        # x = (1 + x) / 2 has fixed point x = 1.
        return [(1, 2)]

    p = target.numerator
    q = target.denominator

    allowed_max_base = min(max_inputs, max_outputs)
    allowed_bases = list(range(2, allowed_max_base + 1))

    bases = find_shortest_base_cycle(q, allowed_bases)

    if bases is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "No exact construction was found under the current feedback template.\n"
            f"target = {target}, q = {q}, allowed_bases = {allowed_bases}\n"
            "In general, q must be coprime to at least one available output count.\n"
            "This does not prove that all logistics structures are impossible; it only means that this feedback template found no construction."
        )

    B = product(bases)

    if (B - 1) % q != 0:
        raise RuntimeError("Internal error: B - 1 is not divisible by q.")

    A = p * (B - 1) // q

    digits = mixed_radix_digits_low_to_high(A, bases)

    pairs = list(zip(digits, bases))

    for r, n in pairs:
        if not (0 <= r <= n - 1):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid digit: r={r}, n={n}")
        if r + 1 > max_inputs:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Input port limit exceeded: r+1={r+1}, max_inputs={max_inputs}")
        if n > max_outputs:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Output port limit exceeded: n={n}, max_outputs={max_outputs}")

    return pairs


def fixed_point_value(pairs: List[Pair]) -> Fraction:
    """
    Verify the closed-loop fixed point.

    If

        u_i = (r_i + u_{i-1}) / n_i,

    then

        u_k = (x + A) / B,

    where

        A = r_1 + r_2 n_1 + r_3 n_1 n_2 + ...
        B = n_1 n_2 ... n_k.

    The fixed point satisfies

        x = A / (B - 1).
    """
    A = 0
    B = 1

    for r, n in pairs:
        A += r * B
        B *= n

    return Fraction(A, B - 1)


def affine_parameters(pairs: List[Pair]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """
    Return A, B such that

        F(x) = (x + A) / B.
    """
    A = 0
    B = 1

    for r, n in pairs:
        A += r * B
        B *= n

    return A, B


def print_solution(target: Fraction, pairs: List[Pair]) -> None:
    A, B = affine_parameters(pairs)
    value = fixed_point_value(pairs)

    print(f"target = {target}")
    print(f"realized = {value}")
    print(f"number of stages = {len(pairs)}")
    print()
    print(f"A = {A}")
    print(f"B = {B}")
    print(f"x = A / (B - 1) = {A} / {B - 1} = {value}")
    print()

    print("(r_i, n_i):")
    for i, (r, n) in enumerate(pairs, start=1):
        print(f"{i:02d}: ({r}, {n})")

    print()
    print("Recurrence:")
    print("u_0 = x")
    for i, (r, n) in enumerate(pairs, start=1):
        print(f"u_{i} = ({r} + u_{i-1}) / {n}")
    print(f"u_{len(pairs)} = u_0 = x")

    print()
    print("LaTeX:")
    print(r"\[")
    print(r"u_0=x,")
    print(r"\qquad")
    for i, (r, n) in enumerate(pairs, start=1):
        comma = "," if i < len(pairs) else "."
        print(rf"u_{{{i}}}=\frac{{{r}+u_{{{i-1}}}}}{{{n}}}{comma}")
    print(r"\]")
    print()
    print(r"\[")
    print(rf"x=\frac{{{A}}}{{{B}-1}}={value.numerator}/{value.denominator}.")
    print(r"\]")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Synthesize round-robin feedback construction for a target duty ratio."
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "target",
        type=str,
        help="Target duty cycle, e.g. 325/799, 1/73, 0.5",
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-inputs",
        type=int,
        default=3,
        help="Maximum input ports per logistics component; default: 3.",
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-outputs",
        type=int,
        default=3,
        help="Maximum output ports per logistics component; default: 3.",
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()

    target = parse_fraction(args.target)

    pairs = synthesize_feedback(
        target=target,
        max_inputs=args.max_inputs,
        max_outputs=args.max_outputs,
    )

    realized = fixed_point_value(pairs)

    if realized != target:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Validation failed: realized={realized}, target={target}")

    print_solution(target, pairs)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
